source.version: Bibliographic metadata only, no abstract and no full text: Crossref record for DOI 10.1007/s10648-026-10217-5 (Educational Psychology Review 38(1), article 128, published 2026-10-03, 220-item reference list read) and OpenAlex record (closed access, no abstract). source.title_on_document: Effects of AI Interventions Across Cognitive, Social-emotional, and Academic Outcomes: a Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials with Nonlinear Dose–response Evidence

supplement.holds: Unknown; the full text was not read.

paper_design_summary: The title describes a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of AI interventions across cognitive, social-emotional, and academic outcomes, with nonlinear dose-response modelling. Whether the review includes non-generative AI is unconfirmed. Its Crossref reference list cites four creativity-related studies (Lee and Chung, 2024; Niloy et al., 2024; Saritepeci and Yildiz Durak, 2024; Urban et al., 2024), but their inclusion in the review and any separate pooled estimate for creativity could not be checked.

eligibility.reason: The Crossref title identifies a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, and OpenAlex W7218618536 classifies it as a review, supporting synthesis context rather than core eligibility. No original randomized people study is identified in the accessible metadata. The title concerns AI interventions across cognitive, social-emotional, and academic outcomes; whether the review includes non-generative AI is unconfirmed. Four creativity-related studies are cited in Crossref reference keys 10217_CR113, 10217_CR143, 10217_CR166, and 10217_CR185, but their inclusion in the review and any creativity-specific pooled estimate are unconfirmed. No abstract or full text was accessible, so study counts, participant counts, output-scored outcomes, and the search end date remain unconfirmed. one_line_finding: A 2026 meta-analysis of randomized trials of AI interventions on cognitive, social-emotional, and academic outcomes (Educational Psychology Review 38, article 128); no pooled number could be confirmed because the abstract and full text were not reachable, and its reference list includes four AI-and-creativity trials (Lee and Chung 2024; Niloy et al. 2024; Saritepeci and Yildiz Durak 2024; Urban et al. 2024).
open_questions: Does the paper report a pooled estimate for creativity or a creativity subgroup, and which trials enter it?
Number of trials and effect sizes, and search end date (one triage screener reported 47 RCTs from the Springer page; not verified here).
notes: Only metadata were read. Semantic Scholar shows a machine-generated TLDR (not the abstract) saying academic outcomes peak at about 22.79 hours of exposure; it was not recorded as a finding because it is not the paper's own text. The candidates note lists Bian et al. 2025 and Li 2023 as creativity trials; the Crossref titles of Bian et al. 2025 (engagement, self-efficacy, cognitive load) and Li 2023 (courseware project performance) do not mention creativity. Full text would need institutional access.
